title: Provisioning docs present UI and as-code setup as peer sections mirroring each other
answers: How should I structure docs when a resource can be set up via UI and via gcx/as-code?
Where should as-code setup instructions for a provisioning method live?
body: Fix pattern: when a resource supports both UI-based and as-code setup, document them as peer H2 sections ('Set up X using the UI' / 'Set up X as code') on the same page rather than only documenting the UI, and factor shared prerequisites (like configuring permitted paths) into a common section referenced by both. Constraints: the as-code section should mirror the structure of the existing Git Sync as-code doc (git-sync/git-sync-setup/set-up-code.md) — create resource YAML, push with gcx, manage with get/edit/delete, verify — for consistency across provisioning docs; add a note mapping UI terminology (e.g. 'local storage') to the actual CRD fields (`spec.type`, `spec.local.path`) so readers don't assume a different/nonexistent schema.
applies: Documentation for any Grafana provisioning/as-code feature that has both a UI wizard and a gcx/Repository-CRD based setup.
says: Where are the code-based setup instructions for this provisioning method?
Documentation should show both UI and code setup methods together.
I need to map UI field names to provisioning field names.
How should we document resources supporting both UI and as-code?
Provisioning documentation lists only UI steps, not code-based steps.
search: When a Grafana resource supports both UI-based and as-code setup, document them as peer H2 sections ('Set up X using the UI' / 'Set up X as code') on the same page with shared prerequisites factored into a common section. The as-code section must mirror the structure of the Git Sync setup docs (git-sync/git-sync-setup/set-up-code.md)—create resource YAML, push with gcx, manage with get/edit/delete, verify—for consistency across provisioning docs. Include an explicit mapping between UI terminology (e.g., 'local storage') and actual CRD fields (spec.type, spec.local.path) to prevent readers from assuming a different schema exists. This pattern applies to documentation for any Grafana provisioning/as-code feature with both a UI wizard and a gcx/Repository-CRD based setup.
